Allah said glory is His lower garment and majesty His cloak, and He will punish whoever contends with Him for them.
Allah forgave a man whom another swore He would not forgive, cancelling the swearer's deeds, and many a dishevelled man turned from doors would have his oath by Allah fulfilled.
The Prophet said that a man who says people are ruined is himself ruined.
Gabriel urged kindness to neighbours on the Prophet so often he thought they would be made heirs, and he told Abu Dharr to add water to his broth for neighbours.
The Prophet told Abu Dharr not to belittle any good, even meeting a brother cheerfully, and bade his Companions speak up for the needy to earn reward.
Good company is like the musk seller, from whom one gains musk or its scent, and bad company like the blacksmith's bellows, which burns clothes or leaves a foul smell.
A woman divided the single date Aisha gave her between her two daughters, eating none, and the Prophet said whoever raises daughters kindly will have protection from Hell.
A mother split the date she meant to eat between her two daughters, earning Paradise, and whoever raises two girls will be close to the Prophet on Resurrection Day.
Parents whose three, or even two, children die, bearing it hoping for reward, are shielded from the Fire, the Prophet told women and a mother who had buried three.
When Allah loves a servant He tells Gabriel, who loves him and announces it in heaven, and he is honoured on earth; Allah's anger spreads the same way.
Souls are gathered troops, the familiar agreeing and the opposed differing, and people are like gold and silver mines, the best before Islam best in it with understanding.
Asked when the Last Hour would come by men whose only preparation was love of Allah and His Messenger, the Prophet said a person will be with those he loves.
Asked about a man who does good and is praised or loved by people for it, the Prophet said it is glad tidings given to a believer in this world.
In the womb, after forty nights or more, an angel writes one's sex, livelihood, deeds, lifespan and fortune unalterably, and destiny may overtake someone a cubit from Paradise or Hell.
Everyone's place in Paradise or Hell is written, the pens having dried; asked why then act, the Prophet said act, for each is eased toward what he was created for.
Moses blamed Adam for bringing people out of Paradise, and Adam prevailed by asking why he blamed him for what Allah had ordained for him before creating him.
Allah set creation's measures fifty thousand years before the heavens and earth, turns all hearts as He wills, and created everything by measure, as revealed when Quraysh disputed about destiny.
Allah has fixed a man's share of adultery: the eye's is the lustful look, the tongue's licentious speech, likewise ears, hands and feet, and the heart yearns.
Every child is born on the fitra, his parents making him a Jew, Christian or Magian; asked about those dying young, the Prophet said Allah knows what they would do.
Asked about polytheists' children, the Prophet said Allah knows what they would do; the youth Khadir killed was a disbeliever by nature, and Allah created Paradise's and Hell's people beforehand.
Umm Habiba prayed to benefit from her husband, father and brother; the Prophet said lifespans and provision are fixed, and metamorphosed people left no offspring, apes and swine predating them.
A strong believer is better and dearer to Allah; seek His help without losing heart, and in trouble do not say 'if only', but that Allah did what He ordained.
Reciting the verse on allegorical verses, the Prophet said to avoid them, angrily said earlier peoples perished disputing over the Book, and bade people recite only while hearts agree.
The Prophet said the most despicable person in Allah's sight is the one who keeps falling into disputes with others.
The Prophet said Muslims would follow the ways of those before them step by step, even into a lizard's hole, and confirmed he meant the Jews and Christians.
The Prophet said three times that those who indulged in hair-splitting were ruined.
Before the Hour knowledge will be taken away, ignorance will prevail, wine will be drunk, adultery, bloodshed and miserliness will spread, and one man will look after fifty women.
Allah removes knowledge by taking the scholars, leaving ignorant leaders who give verdicts without knowledge; Aisha had Urwa ask Abdullah b. Amr again a year later, then accepted it.
Starting a good practice in Islam or calling to righteousness earns the reward of all who follow, and starting an evil practice or calling to error carries their sins.
Allah is as His servant thinks of Him and with him when he remembers Him, drawing nearer as he approaches, and those who remember Allah much have gone ahead.
Allah has ninety-nine names, and whoever memorises or enumerates them will enter Paradise; Allah is Odd and loves odd numbers.
One should supplicate with resolve and conviction, never saying 'forgive me if You wish', for no one can compel Allah and nothing is too great for Him to grant.
None should wish for death over hardship, but may ask to live while life is good and die when death is better; Anas and Khabbab refrained for this reason.
Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him: at death the believer, given glad tidings, loves it, while the disbeliever, told of torment, dislikes it.
Allah is with His servant as he thinks of Him and remembers Him, and draws near him faster than he approaches, rushing to him if he comes walking.
A good deed earns tenfold or more, a bad deed its like or forgiveness, and whoever meets Allah with sins filling the earth, associating none with Him, meets equal pardon.
A sick man had asked to be punished in this world instead of the Hereafter; the Prophet told him to ask for good in both and protection from the Fire.
Roving angels seek out gatherings where Allah is glorified and praised, report their requests to Him, and He forgives them all, even a passer-by who merely sat with them.
The supplication the Prophet made most often asked Allah for good in this world and the Hereafter and protection from the Fire, and Anas included it in all his supplications.
Declaring Allah's oneness, or glorifying and praising Him, a hundred times a day wipes out sins and outweighs other deeds; such words are light on the tongue, dear to Allah.
